lines.text: Mephibosheth was five when he fell, and he spent his whole life afterward waiting for someone to remember him for the wrong reasons.
He lived in a place called Lo-debar - a name that literally means no pasture, nothing growing.
Then a summons came from the king's own house, and he braced for a sword.
Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness, and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
He came in expecting a sentence. He left with a permanent seat at the family table.
Whatever you've been hiding in your own Lo-debar, the door isn't closing. It's opening. In Jesus' name, amen.

bold: a permanent seat at the family table
title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: Thou Shalt Eat Bread at My Table
story: A boy who fell at five grows into a man hidden away in a forgotten village called Lo-debar, then is summoned without warning to the king's own house expecting judgment - and finds a permanent chair waiting for him at the royal table instead, scars and all.
